label: Quarters Arcade
observation: Opened with about 36 games in 2,000 square feet.
interpretation: A dedicated all-ages arcade provides a public gathering point.

label: Another Castle → Town Portal
observation: The historical barcade opened in 2016. A 2024 local retrospective reports that the Another Castle operation was taken over and reopened as Town Portal.
interpretation: This is a documented transition in name and operation, rather than evidence that barcade activity disappeared from the location.
status: Another Castle brand replaced by Town Portal; current Town Portal website lists downtown Bremerton location

label: Ashley’s Pub
observation: A board-game pub opened and later developed a rotating pinball selection.
interpretation: Board-game and pinball activity meet in one venue.

label: Beyond Reality / VR arcade
interpretation: The local scene diversifies into another technology and play format.

label: Tik Tok’s Workshop
observation: A pinball-focused venue opened, linked in the research to an existing collection and repair practice.
interpretation: Technical and collecting activity becomes a permanent public venue.

label: The Game Wizard / Blue Sky Hobbies
observation: Contemporary 2015 reporting places this hobby and game shop across the street from Quarters Arcade.
interpretation: A neighboring tabletop and hobby destination broadens what a visit to the arcade district can include.

label: SEEfilm Cinema
observation: The project author identifies SEEfilm as the nearby movie theater. Contemporary reporting describes cinema, hobby shopping and arcade play as a day of activities on Fourth Street.
interpretation: Film-going is part of the surrounding entertainment ecosystem; no shared ownership or causal link is asserted.

label: Roxy Theatre
observation: The Roxy reopened following renovation in 2018; its current program includes cult, classic, documentary and other screenings.
interpretation: Another cultural destination adds a different form of film-going to the neighborhood.

label: Cafe Omni
observation: Its current official website places Cafe Omni at 206 Burwell Street. The opening year has not been established here.
interpretation: A cafe adds food, rest and informal gathering to the wider scene. It is separate from the unconfirmed upstairs bookshop.

label: Upstairs bookshop
observation: I recall a bookshop above the barcade/hobby corner. Its name, exact location and historical dates still need confirmation.
interpretation: Included as a firsthand research lead rather than an identified, dated business.
